name: Indiana

sales.rateNote: Single statewide 7% gross retail tax; there is no general local sales tax in Indiana, so 7% is the rate everywhere (local food and beverage taxes apply only to prepared food and drinks).

local.levies: no local general sales tax; counties and municipalities that adopt it levy a food and beverage tax on prepared food and drinks (generally 1%, up to 2% where both county and city impose it), plus county innkeeper's taxes on short stays
local.capNote: Food and beverage tax: generally 1% of gross retail income, 2% inside a municipality when county and municipality both adopted it (Commissioner's Directive #30).

groceries.note: Food and food ingredients sold unheated and without utensils are exempt; candy, soft drinks, dietary supplements, alcohol and prepared food are taxable at 7%.

clothing.note: No clothing exemption: clothing is tangible personal property taxed at 7%.

otherRates.item: prepared food and beverages in adopting counties/cities
otherRates.note: Local food and beverage tax of generally 1% (2% where county and city both levy it) on top of the 7% sales tax.

sales.holidayNote: Indiana has no sales tax holiday; none is listed by the Department of Revenue for 2026.

useTax.note: 7% use tax on purchases where at least 7% sales tax was not paid; individuals report it on Form IT-40 (Schedule 4) or on Form ST-115.

facts.text: Indiana's sales tax has been 7% since April 1, 2008 (6% from December 2002 to March 2008); it was first adopted on October 24, 1963.
There is no county or city sales tax: the 7% rate is the same in every store in the state.
Restaurant meals can carry an extra local food and beverage tax of 1%, or 2% where both the county and the city adopted it.
Indiana's candy definition excludes anything with flour on the label or needing refrigeration, so many candy bars are exempt as food.
Remote sellers must register once their Indiana gross revenue exceeds $100,000 in the current or previous calendar year.
Bundled or unitary transactions of seven cents or less are exempt from sales tax.

property.levied: local only: counties, cities and towns, townships, school corporations, libraries and special districts; bills are issued and collected by the county treasurer; the Department of Local Government Finance (DLGF) oversees assessments and budgets

assessment.text: Property is taxed on its net assessed value (gross assessed value minus deductions) times the local rate. Indiana's constitutional circuit-breaker caps limit the bill to 1% of gross assessed value for homesteads, 2% for other residential property and farmland, and 3% for other real and personal property; voter-approved referendum levies sit outside the caps.
assessment.capText: Property is taxed on its net assessed value (gross assessed value minus deductions) times the local rate. Indiana's constitutional circuit-breaker caps limit the bill to 1% of gross assessed value for homesteads, 2% for other residential property and farmland, and 3% for other real and personal property; voter-approved referendum levies sit outside the caps.

homestead.name: Homestead Standard Deduction + Supplemental Homestead Deduction (SEA 1-2025)
homestead.text: Under SEA 1-2025 the standard deduction is fixed at $48,000 for the 2025 assessment date, $40,000 for 2026, $30,000 for 2027, $20,000 for 2028, $10,000 for 2029 and $0 from 2030, while the supplemental homestead deduction rises from 40% of the remaining assessed value (pay 2026) to 66.7% (pay 2031). A Supplemental Homestead Credit of 10% of the homestead tax bill, up to $300, applies automatically from taxes payable in 2026.
homestead.applyBy: File with the county auditor; applications made by January 15 apply to that year's tax bill (e.g. by January 15, 2026 for the 2025 pay 2026 bill). No yearly reapplication.

otherRelief.name: Over 65 Credit
otherRelief.text: SEA 1-2025 replaced the Over 65 Deduction (from the January 1, 2025 assessment date) with a credit of up to $150, subject to income limits (AGI over $60,000 single / $70,000 joint disqualifies).

otherRelief.name: Over 65 Circuit Breaker Credit
otherRelief.text: Eligible seniors' homestead tax cannot rise more than 2% over the previous year.

otherRelief.name: Deduction for 2% circuit breaker properties
otherRelief.text: Automatic deduction for non-homestead residential property, long-term care property and farmland: 6% of AV for 2025 pay 2026, 12% for 2026 pay 2027, rising to 33.4% for 2030 pay 2031.

otherRelief.name: Veterans, blind/disabled and other credits
otherRelief.text: Disabled veteran deductions/credit and blind/disabled credit, filed with the county auditor.

dueDates.text: Property taxes are due twice a year; the statement with the due dates arrives in the spring. Late payment within 30 days: 5% penalty; after 30 days: 10%.

facts.text: Indiana caps homestead tax bills at 1% of gross assessed value, other residential and farmland at 2%, and all other property at 3%.
The 2025 reform (SEA 1) phases the $48,000 homestead standard deduction down to $0 by 2030 while raising the supplemental deduction to 66.7% of assessed value by 2031.
Since taxes payable in 2026, homeowners automatically get a credit of 10% of their homestead tax bill, capped at $300.
Taxes approved by voters in a referendum are outside the 1%/2%/3% caps.
Deductions and credits do not need to be renewed every year, only after a sale or title change.
The Over 65 Deduction was repealed from the January 1, 2025 assessment date and replaced by an Over 65 Credit of up to $150.

uncertain: Exact property tax due dates (customarily May 10 and November 10) were not printed on the DLGF due-date page read; only 'twice a year' was confirmed.
Assessment ratio left null: the DLGF pages read describe gross and net assessed value but no percentage of market value.
No DOR page explicitly stating 'no sales tax holiday'; the holiday note reflects the absence of any holiday in DOR publications.
